transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-08
Start: 14:00 EST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (LumenBank Head of ML), Evan Park (Infra Lead), Sofia Ramirez (CISO)

[00:00] Jared (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros - Jared Kim, I'm the AE on this account; Priya's our solutions eng, she'll drive perf stuff.
[00:12] Maya (LumenBank): Hi - Maya here, thanks. We're exploring options for hosting our inference - leaning toward dedicated capacity to keep isolation and predictable latency.
[00:20] Evan (LumenBank): Evan, infra lead. We need reserved GPUs, options for bursting, and controls for network isolation.
[00:28] Sofia (LumenBank): Sofia, CISO. I may jump in on security and compliance questions.
[00:33] Priya (Redwood): Awesome. Quick agenda: understand current workload, targets (latency, QPS), isolation requirements, and discuss Redwood Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private to see fit.

[01:05] Maya: High-level: we run a customer-facing assistant and a reranker. Peak inference is about 600 qps across models, p95 latency target ~200ms for routing model; cost is a concern but reliability more so.
[01:20] Evan: We're multi-region: NA primary, EU for data residency. We can't send certain PII to hosted multi-tenant endpoints.
[01:31] Jared: Understood - sounds like Dedicated or Private is on the table. Can you share what 'cannot be sent' means exactly? Is it full model access restriction, or just encrypted transit/storage?
[01:44] Sofia: For some products, regulators require that model inputs with account numbers not leave our VPC or be processed by multi-tenant systems. We need KMS, audit logs, and SCIM/SAML SSO and RBAC.
[01:58] Priya: We support VPC peering and private deployments; Dedicated gives you a reserved GPU pool in our infra while still using Redwood control plane, Private gives customer-managed control plane and on-prem options. There are tradeoffs on ops overhead.

[02:30] Evan: For burst, we often have spikes during batch runs and marketing campaigns. How does Redwood handle burst above reserved capacity? Is bursting to hosted allowed or do we need a hard cap?
[02:42] Priya: You can configure burst policies. Typically customers reserve a baseline (e.g., N A100s) and have burst buckets that draw from shared capacity or fall back to queued requests. There is an auto-failover to a compatible model variant if the exact instance isn't available.
[02:58] Maya: Compatible model variant - do you mean a lower-precision quantized variant? We care about quality regression.
[03:06] Priya: Yes, exactly. We can route to a quantized variant with a controlled quality SLA; we also have canary rollouts and A/B so you can measure regressions.

[03:25] Sofia: What's the isolation model? We need tenant-level networking isolation and guarantees that no other tenant's kernels share the same GPU.
[03:34] Priya: For Dedicated, GPUs are isolated to your pool. We do host-level tenant isolation and optionally single-tenant hosts for stricter requirements. The more strict, the higher the price. There are also controls for kernel-level isolation and encrypted KV cache.
[03:50] Evan: Kernel-level isolation - any noisy neighbor risk? We've seen issues on generic cloud multi-tenant GPU instances.
[03:58] Priya: Our runtime schedules workloads and enforces eviction and slotting policies; for Dedicated pools we have strict tenancy, and we can provision physical hosts per customer for stronger isolation.

[04:18] Jared: Quick question - regarding caching and KV cache, do you encrypt caches with customer KMS?
[04:24] Priya: Yes, for Dedicated and Private we integrate with customer KMS, HSMs for keys, and data at rest is encrypted. There can be slight perf differences when using external KMS calls, but we can do envelope keys to mitigate latency.

[04:46] Maya: Great. On sizing, any rules of thumb for mapping qps to GPU counts?
[04:53] Priya: It depends heavily on model, sequence length, and batchability. Typical LLM rerankers at 1k-token budget might do X qps per A100 - we usually run a benchmark. For 600 qps across two models, a starting baseline might be 4-8 GPUs with autoscale for burst; but we need to benchmark your models and prompts.
[05:15] Evan: We prefer a predictable SLA with known p95 latency. Can Redwood provide latency SLOs for Dedicated?
[05:22] Jared: We do SLA-backed latency targets for Dedicated packages; we'll share sample SLOs.

[05:35] Maya: Any constraints about model size? Our primary model is a 70B open model, quantized. We also keep a smaller 7B for lower-latency cases.
[05:46] Priya: We support large models and quantized runtimes; for 70B you'll want GPUs with sufficient memory or multi-GPU sharding. We recommend profiling during the pilot.

[06:10] Evan: About pricing: how does reserved capacity pricing differ from hosted? Are there commitments and minimums?
[06:19] Jared: Dedicated is a reserved monthly commit, often with tiers (e.g., 4 x A100 reserved). We offer burst credits and committed usage discounts. We'll send the pricing deck; commitments and term lengths affect discounts.

[06:35] Sofia: From security side: provide SOC 2, ISO, penetration test reports, and details on key management and audit logging. Also want to review data retention and deletion flows.
[06:45] Priya: We'll share SOC 2 and our security whitepaper. For data retention, logs are configurable and we can route audit logs to your SIEM via secure forwarding.

[07:01] Maya: Operationally, what does deployment look like? How long to get a Dedicated pool provisioned?
[07:07] Priya: Typical lead time is a few days to a couple of weeks depending on region and host type; single-tenant bare-metal takes longer. We can provide a pilot in 1-2 weeks for an initial benchmark on shared Dedicated hosts.

[07:25] Evan: We also want to understand upgrade/rollout strategies: model version pinning, rollback, canaries.
[07:33] Priya: Redwood Console supports rollouts with canary percentages, automatic fallback to previous model variants on errors, and per-route dashboards. We'll share example configs.

[07:50] Maya: For the pilot we want 4 GPUs baseline, ability to burst to 8 for short windows, full KV cache support, KMS integration, and audit logs.
[07:59] Jared: Sounds good. Priya, can we run a 4->8 benchmark using LumenBank's model and a traffic replay?
[08:06] Priya: Yes - we'll need a sample workload and representative prompts. We can do a 4-hour perf run and capture p50/p95 and cost metrics.

[08:20] Maya: We'll provide traffic and a few evaluation prompts.
[08:23] Sofia: Also confirm we can enforce EU residency for EU traffic.
[08:27] Priya: Yes, we can route by region and provide EU-only Dedicated pools. There may be slight capacity lead times.

[08:40] Evan: Any dependencies on our side? Firewall rules, peering, VPC setup?
[08:45] Priya: We'll work with infra to set up VPC peering, define allowed CIDR blocks, and arrange mutual TLS for service endpoints if needed. We'll send a network checklist.

[08:58] Jared: Quick product note - we can support on-prem private deployment if regulatory requirements demand. That's a heavier lift but available.
[09:06] Maya: For now Dedicated in-hosted regions with VPC peering should be fine; we'll escalate to Private if auditors require it.

[09:20] Sofia: Contractually, we need data processing addendum, breach notification timelines, and clear SLAs.
[09:27] Jared: Noted - we'll include DPA language in the sample contract.

[09:40] Priya: I'll lead the benchmark. If we see consistent regressions on quantized variants, we can recommend different batching or kernel options. Also will test KV cache hit rates.

[10:00] Maya: Sounds good. Any questions from your side, Evan?
[10:05] Evan: No more right now. I'm most concerned about burst predictability and cost modeling during peak campaigns.

[10:15] Jared: Final recap - action items: Jared send pricing and contract sample; Priya run perf benchmark after we get traffic; LumenBank provide workload; Sofia to confirm compliance docs needed; schedule follow-up with legal.
[10:31] Maya: Thanks, appreciate the clarity.
[10:34] Sofia: Thanks. We'll loop in procurement after the benchmark.
[10:38] Jared: Great. We'll follow up with the deck and security docs today and propose benchmark slots. Thanks everyone.

End of call.
